questions.question: According to the law of constant proportion, what will be the correct ratio of obtained oxygen and hydrogen (O : H) after decomposition of 18 g water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16:2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the law of constant proportion, a chemical compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• Water (H₂O) is composed of hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio of 2:16 by mass.
 
• The molar mass of water is 18 g/mol, with oxygen contributing 16 g/mol and hydrogen contributing 2 g/mol.
 
• Upon decomposition of 18 g of water, 16 g of oxygen and 2 g of hydrogen will be obtained.
 
• This ratio of the mass of oxygen to hydrogen (O:H) after decomposition is 16:2, confirming the law of constant proportion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**

 
 
• This law states that if two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass**
 
 
• This law states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
 
 
• **Law of Definite Composition**
 
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains the same elements in the exact same proportions by mass.

questions.question: Which of the following is the molecular mass of HNO₃?

The correct answer is __**63 u**__.

__

• This makes the molecular mass of HNO₃ equal to 63 u.
 
• Therefore, the correct option is 1, which corresponds to 63 u.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u)**

 
 
• It is a standard unit of mass that quantifies mass on an atomic or molecular scale (atomic mass).
 
• One atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a single carbon-12 atom.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass**
 
 
• The molecular mass of a substance is the mass of one molecule of that substance, measured in atomic mass units (u).
 
• It is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Molecular Mass**
 
 
• To calculate the molecular mass, identify the number of atoms of each element in the molecule.
 
• Multiply the atomic mass of each element by the number of atoms of that element.
 
• Add the results to obtain the molecular mass.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the ratio by mass of hydrogen to oxygen atoms (H:O) in a water molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1:8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A water molecule (H₂O) consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• The atomic mass of hydrogen is approximately 1 u (atomic mass unit), and the atomic mass of oxygen is approximately 16 u.
 
• Therefore, the total mass of the hydrogen atoms in a water molecule is 2 u (2 hydrogen atoms × 1 u).
 
• The mass of the oxygen atom in a water molecule is 16 u.
 
• The ratio by mass of hydrogen to oxygen atoms in a water molecule is thus 2:16, which simplifies to 1:8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Molecule Structure**

 
 
• Water is a polar molecule, with the oxygen atom having a partial negative charge and the hydrogen atoms having partial positive charges.
 
• This polarity leads to hydrogen bonding between water molecules, which gives water its unique properties such as high surface tension and boiling point.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonding**
 
 
• Hydrogen bonds are weak bonds that form between the hydrogen atom of one water molecule and the oxygen atom of another water molecule.
 
• These bonds are responsible for many of water's unusual properties, including its high specific heat capacity and its role as a universal solvent.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Water**
 
 
• Water is essential for life, serving as a solvent, a temperature buffer, and a reactant in various biochemical processes.
 
• It is also used in numerous industrial applications, including cooling, cleaning, and as a raw material in chemical reactions.

questions.question: Which of the following is the formulas unit mass of NaCl?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**58.5 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula unit mass of a compound is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in its formula.
 
• Sodium (Na) has an atomic mass of approximately 23 u (atomic mass units).
 
• Chlorine (Cl) has an atomic mass of approximately 35.5 u.
 
• Therefore, the formula unit mass of NaCl is calculated by adding the atomic masses of Na and Cl.
 
• The calculation is: 23 u (Na) + 35.5 u (Cl) = 58.5 u.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Mass**

 
 
• It is the mass of an atom, usually expressed in atomic mass units (u).
 
• The atomic mass is roughly equal to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass**
 
 
• It is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
• Molecular mass is often used for covalently bonded molecules, such as H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Formula Unit**
 
 
• A formula unit is the empirical formula of an ionic or covalent network solid compound used as an independent entity for stoichiometric calculations.
 
• For ionic compounds like NaCl, the formula unit represents the simplest ratio of the ions involved.

questions.question: In case of jelly, which of the following is the dispersed phase?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liquid phase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In jelly, the dispersed phase is the **liquid phase** while the dispersion medium is the solid phase.
 
• Jelly is a type of **gel** where the liquid phase is dispersed in the solid network.
 
• The liquid phase in jelly provides the fluidity and moisture content of the gel.
 
• During the jelly-making process, the liquid phase solidifies upon cooling, forming a semi-solid structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersed Phase:**

 
 
• The dispersed phase refers to the phase that is distributed or spread throughout another continuous phase known as the dispersion medium.
 
• In the context of colloids, the dispersed phase can be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion Medium:**
 
 
• The dispersion medium is the continuous phase in which the dispersed phase is distributed.
 
• The dispersion medium can also be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
 
 
• **Colloids:**
 
 
• Colloids are mixtures where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another without dissolving.
 
• Common types of colloids include gels, sols, emulsions, and foams.
 
 
 
• **Gel:**
 
 
• A gel is a colloidal system in which the dispersed phase is a liquid and the dispersion medium is a solid.
 
• Gels exhibit a semi-solid state and have properties of both solids and liquids.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding metals?

options.text: Metals are good conductors of heat.
Metals have to be drawn into thin wires.
Lead and mercury are comparatively good conductors of heat.
Surface of metals in their pure state is shiny.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Metals are generally good conductors of heat due to the free movement of electrons within their structure.
 
• Metals can be drawn into thin wires, a property known as ductility.
 
• Lead and mercury are comparatively poor conductors of heat when compared to other metals like copper and aluminum.
 
• Lead and mercury are poor conductors of heat because they have relatively few free electrons available for conducting thermal energy, and their atomic structures (heavy atomic mass for lead and liquid state for mercury at room temperature) do not facilitate efficient energy transfer through lattice vibrations or electron movements.
 
• Metals, in their pure state, typically exhibit a shiny, lustrous surface.
 
• Conductivity of heat in metals is crucial for their use in various industrial applications such as cookware and heat exchangers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Metals**

 
 
• Metals are malleable, meaning they can be hammered or rolled into thin sheets.
 
• Most metals have high melting and boiling points.
 
 
 
• **Alloys**
 
 
• Alloys are mixtures of two or more elements, with at least one being a metal, to enhance properties such as strength and resistance to corrosion.
 
• Common examples include steel (iron and carbon) and bronze (copper and tin).
 
 
 
• **Non-metals**
 
 
• Non-metals are elements that lack the properties of metals and are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• Examples include sulfur, phosphorus, and carbon (in the form of graphite).

questions.question: Which of the following metals are mixed with iron to get stainless steel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nickel and chromium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Stainless steel is primarily made by mixing iron with chromium and nickel to enhance its properties.
 
• Chromium is added to stainless steel to improve its corrosion resistance and to create a passive layer that prevents rust.
 
• Nickel is added to increase the toughness and strength of stainless steel, especially at low temperatures.
 
• Stainless steel is widely used in various applications due to its durability, resistance to corrosion, and aesthetic appearance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Stainless Steel**

 
 
• There are different types of stainless steel, including austenitic, ferritic, martensitic, and duplex, each with unique properties and applications.
 
• Austenitic stainless steel is the most common type, known for its excellent corrosion resistance and formability.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Stainless Steel**
 
 
• Stainless steel is used in a wide range of industries, including construction, automotive, medical, and food processing.
 
• Its resistance to corrosion makes it ideal for kitchen appliances, cutlery, and surgical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Maintenance of Stainless Steel**
 
 
• Regular cleaning and maintenance can help preserve the appearance and longevity of stainless steel products.
 
• Using mild detergents and avoiding abrasive cleaners will prevent damage to the passive layer of stainless steel.

questions.question: Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon. This property is known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Catenation** is the unique ability of carbon to form bonds with other carbon atoms.
 
• This property allows carbon to form long chains, branched molecules, and complex structures such as rings.
 
• Catenation is a significant reason for the vast number of organic compounds.
 
• Carbon-carbon bonds are strong and stable, facilitating the formation of a wide variety of molecular structures.
 
• The ability of carbon to catenate is due to its tetravalent nature, allowing it to form up to four covalent bonds with other atoms, including other carbon atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allotropes**

 
 
• These are different forms of the same element, where the atoms are bonded together in different ways. For example, carbon has several allotropes, including diamond, graphite, and graphene.
 
 
 
• **Homologous Series**
 
 
• A homologous series is a group of organic compounds with a similar general formula, varying by a CH₂ unit. They have similar chemical properties and show a gradation in physical properties.
 
 
 
• **Cyclisation**
 
 
• This refers to the process of forming a ring structure from a chain of atoms. Cyclisation is common in organic chemistry for forming cyclic compounds.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5.
When pH of rain water is less than 5.6, it is called acid rain.
Living organisms can survive only in a narrow range of pH change.
When pH of rain water is more than 5.6, it is called acid rain.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5. This is because acidic conditions can erode the enamel on teeth.
 
• When the pH of rainwater is less than 5.6, it is referred to as acid rain. This occurs due to the presence of sulfuric and nitric acids in the atmosphere.
 
• Living organisms can survive only in a narrow range of pH change, as extreme pH levels can disrupt biological processes.
 
• When the pH of rainwater is more than 5.6, it is not considered acid rain. Therefore, option 4 is incorrect.
 
• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral. Below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic (alkaline).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acid Rain**

 
 
• Acid rain can have harmful effects on plants, aquatic animals, and infrastructure.
 
• It is primarily caused by emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) which react with water molecules in the atmosphere to produce acids.
 
 
 
• **pH in Human Body**
 
 
• The human body maintains a tightly regulated pH level in the blood, typically around 7.4, which is slightly alkaline.
 
• Enzymatic activities within the body are highly sensitive to changes in pH.
 
 
 
• **Buffer Solutions**
 
 
• Buffer solutions are used to maintain a stable pH in a system, even when small amounts of acid or base are added.
 
• They are essential in many biochemical and industrial processes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct according to the law of conservation of mass?

options.text: Mass can be created but cannot be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be created in a chemical reaction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• This principle was established by Antoine Lavoisier in the 18th century.
 
• In a closed system, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
 
• The law applies to both physical changes and chemical reactions.
 
• This law is fundamental to the field of chemistry and underpins stoichiometric calculations in chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions**

 
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• It is also known as Proust's law.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**
 
 
• This law states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
• It was formulated by John Dalton.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry**
 
 
• It involves the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• It is based on the laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions.

questions.question: Which of the following metals CANNOT be cut with a knife?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium, lithium, and potassium are alkali metals that are soft and can be cut with a knife.
 
• Alkali metals are known for their softness and low density.
 
• Copper is a transition metal, which is much harder and cannot be cut with a knife.
 
• The hardness of a metal is determined by its atomic structure and bonding.
 
• Alkali metals have a single electron in their outer shell, which makes them highly reactive and soft.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkali Metals**

 
 
• These metals are found in Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• They are highly reactive, especially with water, and are stored in oil to prevent reactions with moisture in the air.
 
• Examples include lithium, sodium, and potassium.
 
 
 
• **Transition Metals**
 
 
• These metals are found in the central block of the periodic table (Groups 3-12).
 
• They are characterized by their ability to form variable oxidation states and colored compounds.
 
• Examples include copper, iron, and gold.
 
 
 
• **Metals and Their Properties**
 
 
• Metals are generally malleable, ductile, and good conductors of electricity and heat.
 
• The physical properties of metals vary widely across the periodic table.
 
• Reactivity, hardness, and melting points of metals can differ significantly based on their atomic structure and bonding.

questions.question: Why do covalently bonded compounds have low boiling point?

options.text: Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have weak covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have strong covalent bond within molecules and also strong intermolecular force
Have strong intermolecular force within molecules but weak covalent bond

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Covalently bonded compounds have strong covalent bonds within the molecules, which keep the atoms together in a molecule.
 
• Despite strong intramolecular forces, these compounds exhibit weak intermolecular forces between different molecules.
 
• The weak intermolecular forces (like van der Waals forces) require less energy to break, leading to a lower boiling point.
 
• These compounds usually exist in the form of gases or liquids at room temperature due to their low boiling points.
 
• Examples of covalently bonded compounds with low boiling points include molecular hydrogen (H₂), nitrogen (N₂), and methane (CH₄).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intermolecular Forces**

 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion which act between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Types of intermolecular forces include dipole-dipole interactions, London dispersion forces, and hydrogen bonding.
 
 
 
• **Boiling Point**
 
 
• The boiling point of a substance is the temperature at which its vapor pressure equals the external pressure surrounding the liquid.
 
• Strong intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point as more energy is required to separate the molecules.
 
 
 
• **Polar and Non-Polar Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• Polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared unequally between atoms, leading to a distribution of charge.
 
• Non-polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared equally, resulting in no overall charge distribution.

questions.question: How many electrons does carbon typically share when bonding with another carbon atom or with atoms of other elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons in its outer shell.
 
• To achieve a full outer shell, carbon typically forms four covalent bonds.
 
• When bonding with another carbon atom or with other elements, carbon shares four electrons.
 
• This allows carbon to create a wide variety of compounds with different elements.
 
• The versatility of carbon in forming bonds is fundamental to organic chemistry and the structure of biological molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Covalent Bonds**

 
 
• A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
 
• Covalent bonding is common in organic molecules where carbon atoms form stable bonds with other carbon atoms or different elements like hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons**
 
 
• Valence electrons are the outermost electrons of an atom and are involved in forming bonds.
 
• The number of valence electrons determines the bonding behavior of an element.
 
 
 
• **Organic Chemistry**
 
 
• Organic chemistry is the study of the structure, properties, composition, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds containing carbon atoms.
 
• Carbon's ability to form stable bonds with many elements, including itself, makes it unique and essential for life.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules has triple bond between the two atoms?

• **Cl₂ (Chlorine)**
 
 
• Contains a single bond between two chlorine atoms.
 
• It is used in water purification and as a disinfectant.

• It is essential for respiration in most living organisms.

options.text: Sodium carbonate is used in glass, soap and paper industries.
Sodium carbonate is used in the manufacture of sodium compounds, such as borax.
Sodium carbonate is used to neutralise excess acid in the stomach.
Sodium carbonate can be used as a cleaning agent for domestic purposes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium carbonate(Na₂Co₃), also known as soda ash or washing soda, is widely used in the glass, soap, and paper industries.
 
• It is utilized in the manufacture of various sodium compounds, such as borax.
